title: Fail the session cookie safe to Secure in production

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0070 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y a lo que sigue' — the fourth hardening fix, closing the cookie-Secure-default finding per the owner's explicit policy choice. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0070.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: The hardening audit found the session cookie could be issued without the Secure flag under the default COOKIE_SECURE='auto' when TRUST_PROXY is unset: 'auto' uses req.secure, which is false behind a TLS-terminating proxy that has not been trusted, so a production cookie could be sent over plain HTTP.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/http.ts secureCookie prior behavior; the 2026-08-24 hardening-audit finding hardening-cookie-secure-default.

claims.statement: The owner chose the fail-safe-to-Secure policy (over warn-only or require-explicit): in production, COOKIE_SECURE='auto' resolves to 'always' so the session cookie is always Secure, and deployments behind a TLS-terminating proxy must set TRUST_PROXY and serve HTTPS. The change resolves this at config load via a pure resolveCookieSecure helper and documents TRUST_PROXY and the fail-safe in .env.example.
claims.evidence: AskUserQuestion answer on 2026-08-24; server/src/config/environment.ts resolveCookieSecure; server/.env.example.

claims.statement: Governed discovery resolved the fail-safe at the config layer (auto to always in production) rather than threading a production flag through the cookie helpers, which keeps http.ts a pure request-scoped module and makes the resolution directly testable.
claims.evidence: server/src/config/environment.ts resolveCookieSecure is a pure exported function; server/src/auth/http.ts is unchanged.

claims.statement: Asserting resolveCookieSecure('auto','production') is 'always' (and that explicit modes and development 'auto' are unchanged), plus that setSessionCookie with 'always' sets Secure regardless of req.secure, proves the fail-safe.

The fail-safe makes the cookie Secure, not the transport HTTPS — a plain-HTTP production deployment will break logins because a Secure cookie is not sent over HTTP. This is the intended forcing function: operators set TRUST_PROXY and serve HTTPS, or set COOKIE_SECURE='never' for local non-HTTPS development.
claims.evidence: server/.env.example guidance; the SameSite=Strict Secure cookie semantics.

claims.statement: Human review accepted CHG-0070: in production, COOKIE_SECURE='auto' resolves to 'always' so the session cookie is always Secure, closing the misconfigured-proxy downgrade; TRUST_PROXY and the fail-safe are documented. This was the owner's explicit policy choice; it forces HTTPS in production.
claims.evidence: server/src/config/environment.ts, server/.env.example, server/tests/unit/cookieSecure.test.ts, the passing full server suite under npm run check, the CHG-0070 pull-request Constitution run (8 jobs green), and human acceptance on 2026-08-24.

claims.statement: The change is server-only: a config resolution, an .env.example doc, and a test. No protocol or Studio change and no existing behavior regresses (development and test environments keep the raw mode).
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0070 branch: server/src/config/environment.ts, server/.env.example and server/tests/unit/cookieSecure.test.ts.

successCriteria.statement: In production, COOKIE_SECURE='auto' resolves so the session cookie is always Secure; explicit modes and development 'auto' are unchanged.
successCriteria.verification: A test asserts resolveCookieSecure('auto','production') is 'always', ('auto','development') is 'auto', and 'always'/'never' are returned unchanged.

successCriteria.statement: The resolved mode produces a Secure cookie regardless of the request's TLS state.
successCriteria.verification: A test asserts setSessionCookie with 'always' sets secure true even when req.secure is false, while 'auto' follows req.secure and 'never' is never Secure.

successCriteria.statement: TRUST_PROXY and the fail-safe are documented and no existing behavior regresses.
successCriteria.verification: server/.env.example documents TRUST_PROXY and the production fail-safe; the full server suite passes.

definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.
